questions.q: The lines $xcos\alpha + ysin\alpha = P, \alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ are chords of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x2}{9} - \dfrac{y2}{36} = 1$& and they subtend a right angle at the centre of the hyperbola. The locus of the poles of these lines with respect to the given hyperbola is
questions.solution:
The equation of the straight lines joining origin to the points of intersection of the line $xcos\alpha + ysin\alpha = P$ and the hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{36} = 1$ can be obtained by making the equation of the hyperbola homogeneous.

For this, we have from the equation of the line, i.e. $xcos\alpha + ysin\alpha = P$

$⇒ \dfrac{xcos\alpha + ysin\alpha}{P} = 1 .$

Put, this value in the equation of hyperbola, i.e.

$\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{36} = {\left(1\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{36} = {\left(\dfrac{xcos\alpha + ysin\alpha}{P}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{36} = \dfrac{{x}^{2}{cos}^{2}\alpha + {y}^{2}{sin}^{2}\alpha + 2xycos\alphasin\alpha}{{P}^{2}}$

$⇒ {x}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{{cos}^{2}\alpha}{{P}^{2}}\right) + {y}^{2}\left(- \dfrac{1}{36} - \dfrac{{sin}^{2}\alpha}{{P}^{2}}\right) - \dfrac{2xycos\alphasin\alpha}{{P}^{2}} = 0 .$

This is equation will represent a pair of perpendicular straight lines, if, the sum of coefficients of ${x}^{2}$ and ${y}^{2}$ is zero.

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{{cos}^{2}\alpha}{{P}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{36} - \dfrac{{sin}^{2}\alpha}{{P}^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ {P}^{2} = 12$

$⇒ P = \pm 2\sqrt{3} .$

Hence, the chords of the hyperbola are $xcos\alpha + ysin\alpha = \pm 2\sqrt{3} . . . \left(i\right)$

Let, the poles of these lines with respect to the given hyperbola is $A\left(h, k\right) .$

Then, we know that the equation of the polar for a point $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ to the hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ is $\dfrac{x \cdot {x}_{1}}{{a}^{2}} - \dfrac{y \cdot {y}_{1}}{{b}^{2}} = 1 .$

Thus, the equation of the polar for the point $A\left(h, k\right)$ to the hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{9} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{36} = 1$ or $4{x}^{2} - {y}^{2} = 36$ is

$4hx - ky = 36 . . . \left(ii\right)$

On comparing the equations $\left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right),$ we get

$\dfrac{4h}{cos\alpha} = \dfrac{- k}{sin\alpha} = \dfrac{36}{\pm 2\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ cos\alpha = \pm \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}h}{9}, sin\alpha = ∓ \dfrac{\sqrt{3}k}{18}$

Using ${cos}^{2}\alpha + {sin}^{2}\alpha = 1,$ we get

$⇒ {\left(\pm \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}h}{9}\right)}^{2} + {\left(∓ \dfrac{\sqrt{3}k}{18}\right)}^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{12{h}^{2}}{81} + \dfrac{3{k}^{2}}{324} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{4{h}^{2}}{27} + \dfrac{{k}^{2}}{108} = 1$

$⇒ 16{h}^{2} + {k}^{2} = 108 .$

Hence, the locus is obtained by replacing $\left(h, k\right)$ by $\left(x, y\right) .$

Thus, the required locus is $16{x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 108 .$

& =$\frac{13}{k}$\\
